description: Wako leg remesh + toe-bone flip, ROUND 4 (wako_mesh_rebuild.py revision 4): ball-and-socket hip, 7-loop knee with rigid back crease, 5-loop crouch-proof ankle, forefoot toe cap.  Body/head vertices, faces and UVs untouched; 9 bones (only toe.L/toe.R rest changed), 33 actions unchanged.

summary.whole_mesh_symmetry_error_m_note: body itself is asymmetric by up to 0.45 mm in the original (unchanged)

triangle_budget.note: about 370 triangles per leg are the hip ball + socket; roughly half of that (lining and fold band, ~370 in total) is never visible (inside the body).  Target was ~2600: the build is +6.7 % over it for the ball-and-socket hip, which removes every visible hip crater / slit / shear at all hip angles.

leg_face_quality.note: tube faces below the rim only (all quads); the socket/ball bands are emitted as explicitly triangulated strips (matching diagonals) and fan transitions

hip_decision.decision: geometric fix, no runtime hip-flexion cap needed
hip_decision.how: the thigh carries a sphere about the hip pivot (R 0.138 m) seated in a root-weighted socket inside the body; rotations about the pivot map the ball onto itself, so the opening always shows rigid ball surface.  The root->thigh weight change sits on a fold band at the ball's front-top.
hip_decision.valid_range_note: the fold cap (radius 14 deg) lies inside the 22 deg cap that no pose in this range turns into the opening (55 deg view window); beyond it the hidden fold band could come into view
hip_decision.visible_result: flexion shows the ball turning inside a round socket throat (3.5-4 mm seam, a light countersink bevel at the octagon corners) and a smooth 3 cm 'seat' bulge below the body at hip 90-120; no blended skin, crater, slit or fold at any hip angle

godot_import_check.note: only toe.L / toe.R rests differ (the designed 180 deg flip); all other rests are bit-identical

deformation.review_harness: mesh_work4/ev4.py: review posing convention (critic_render/intersect scripts); per pose: total volume change (divergence theorem, both legs), dominant-bone triangle-pair intersection census, knee bisector cut depth, and orthographic rasters of the views the review used: visible back faces (fold-overs, see-through in Godot), visible surface other than the original body skin more than 5 mm inside the rest body hull (areas summed over the views of each pose; for the final build this is the rigid ball inside the round socket throat and the socket bevel), the same restricted to BLENDED (deforming) skin -- the review's crater / slit / pocket -- and silhouette slots narrower than 2.4 cm.  3 mm pixels.
notes: knee bisector depth 0.199 / 0.200 m at 60 / 90 deg (round 3: 0.180 / 0.169, original 0.186 / 0.198) with the 145 deg front line still <= 1.97x stretch and 18.5 deg turn change

shin x thigh pairs at 120-145 deg are a rigid back-of-thigh / back-of-shin contact line (two 20 cm tubes folded to 35-60 deg must overlap); the count scales with tessellation (16 vs 8 sides in the original)

the ankle front of a flat-foot crouch is a closed crease: the folded skin lies between the two rigid surfaces, so the front-line turn reads ~170 deg while the visible silhouette has no slot: the remaining 4.1 mm 'notch' is the designed toe-cap groove itself (same at rest)

silhouette_slot_px at tuck [side] is 144 px (orig 61, round 3 58): it is the open wedge between the tucked foot's instep and the rigid ball 'seat' under the body (two separate parts, see mesh_work4 evimg), not a skin slit; crouch90 / crouch120 side slots are 42 / 82 px (orig 44 / 76, round 3 90 / 138): the natural back-of-knee and front-of-ankle wedges, with no hooked ankle slot
volume numbers count interpenetrating regions twice (divergence theorem); hip poses are now exact (rigid ball), e.g. hip -35: 0 cm3 (round 3: -1460, original -278)

godot_lod_check.how: RenderingServer.mesh_get_surface(...).lods of the imported wakoMesh (Godot's default generate_lods); visual check renders/deformation/godot_lod_check_before_after.jpg forces coarser LODs at close range with Viewport.mesh_lod_threshold 8 and 24 px (default 1)
godot_lod_check.result: at 8 px the after mesh reads like LOD0 (ball, socket and knee intact); at a forced 24 px both meshes facet and the after tuck knee shows small cracks along the back crease -- only reached when Wako is small on screen at the default 1 px threshold

toe_animation_check.method: 33 actions evaluated at 7 frames each in the original and rebuilt files; toe tail displacement relative to the foot, projected on the toe's own pointing direction and on world up
toe_animation_check.conclusion: the flip is a rigid Rz(pi) pre-multiply of the rest frame: local-X rotation keys still curl/lift the tip in the same sense along the toe, local-Y location keys still retract along it; the existing toe channels are NOT reversed and re-authoring must not invert them

runtime_toe_frame_consumers: wako_helper.gd:1336-1337, 1359-1361, 1380 -- tool anchor basis built from toe.basis.x / toe.basis.y; grip = toe.origin + toe.basis.y*0.035; tool tip along toe.basis.y
wako_pose.gd:496-500, 529 -- foot-held grip offset toe.basis.y*0.035 in the foot frame; :1850 aligns toe.basis.y to the work axis

wako_back_tool.gd:437-540, 654, 752, 848-1170 -- toe frame (_toe, _toe_in_ankle, home toe) drives waypoints, routes, turn rates and clearances; 946-955 tilt from _toe.basis.y; 1102 grip_offset 0.035+size.y*0.45; 1500, 1510, 1674-1677 tool frame from toe.basis.y
wako_pickup.gd:81, 94 -- grip.origin + grip.basis.y*0.035 contact test and foot anchor
wako_portable_gun.gd:87 -- gun grip frame from toe.basis and toe.basis.y*0.035

NOTE: with the flip both toe.basis.x and toe.basis.y are negated (Godot): every foot-held tool, gun control and cargo anchor built from the toe frame turns 180 deg about vertical until these consumers are retuned; the grip point (head + 0.035 along +Y, at y 0.095 / z 0.049) now lies about 2 cm inside the toe pad's front face (front of the foot at y 0.119 m)

runtime_benchmark.setup: 64 instances playing wk_run, identical untextured material, Godot 4.7.1 Forward+ on lavapipe (software Vulkan, shared CPU), 640x360, frames 41-240, 2 interleaved runs per mesh (before = original Wako.blend, after = round-4 Wako.blend) while other jobs loaded the machine (load averages after each run: 37.90, 34.07, 34.37; 33.36, 33.40, 34.13; 31.88, 33.06, 33.99; 27.34, 31.85, 33.54)
runtime_benchmark.note: noisy on a shared CPU.  Median frame time before [84.04, 84.056] ms, after [110.772, 115.959] ms: after is ~35 % slower in this software-rasterised, CPU-skinned setup (1674 vs 792 GPU vertices, 2774 vs 1110 triangles), which does not predict GPU cost.  primitives_in_frame depends on Godot's auto-generated mesh LODs and shadow culling, so it is not 2x the triangle count.  Round 3 (1484 GPU vertices / 2550 triangles) measured ~10-15 % slower than the original in the same setup.
